rawFindings.title: Incorrect expected brace logic introduced in curly.js
rawFindings.explanation: The existing code correctly set `expected` to true if the first statement within the block has leading comments, which influences brace enforcement correctly under `multi-or-nest` option for a block with exactly one statement. The change unconditionally sets `expected = false`, removing this conditional logic. This will cause the rule to behave incorrectly for cases where braces are expected due to leading comments inside single-statement blocks under `multi-or-nest` option.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original logic: assign `expected = leadingComments.length > 0;` instead of `expected = false;` to preserve intended behavior.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange:
Input code: `if (foo) { // some comment
 bar(); }` with options `['multi-or-nest']` will incorrectly report or fail to enforce expected braces because `expected` is always false now. The previous logic correctly handled this by requiring braces in this case.
